intro.text:
Phone Shop Manager: wireframe of the whole app.

These are simple sketches of every screen, without final colours or design. Read them row by row, from top to bottom. The yellow notes explain each part in plain words. All names and numbers are only examples.

The app is a template: shop name, logo, currency, tax and product categories are all set in Settings, so any phone shop can use it.

Look and feel (updated): soft gradient backgrounds, frosted-glass cards and bars, a purple-to-teal gradient on main buttons, and gentle motion. Cards float in when a screen opens, buttons press in, charts grow, and the Add button softly glows. Motion switches off automatically for people who turn animations off. The default currency is LKR (Sri Lanka), and the owner can change it in setup and Settings.

Leave a comment on anything you want changed.

s0.text:
First time only: a setup wizard asks for the shop name, logo, currency, tax and which money accounts you use.

Then each person logs in with their own account.

Home shows today at a glance, with big buttons for the jobs you do most. 'More' opens every part of the app.

The cloud sign: 'Saved online' means everything is safe in Supabase. 'Waiting for internet' means it will upload by itself later.

s1.text:
Products list with search, category filter and a low-stock warning.

Adding a product asks different questions for each category: a phone asks for IMEI, storage, RAM and condition; a cover asks which models it fits.

Phones are tracked one by one by IMEI, from the supplier to the customer.

You can add your own categories and questions in Settings.

s2.text:
How a sale works:
1. Add items to the cart (search or scan a barcode).
2. Choose the customer and take payment. You can split it (part cash, part bank) or take part payment. Whatever is unpaid becomes the customer's debt automatically.
3. Share the bill on WhatsApp or print it.

Returns and trade-ins (taking a used phone from a customer) are here too.

s3.text:
How a repair works:
1. Make a job card when a phone comes in: the problem, pattern lock, advance paid and promised date.
2. Move it through the steps: Received, Checking, Waiting for parts, Repairing, Ready, Delivered.
3. Spare parts used come out of stock and count against the job's profit.
4. Send 'your phone is ready' on WhatsApp, then deliver it and take the balance.

s4.text:
How buying works:
1. Make a purchase order and send it to the supplier on WhatsApp.
2. When the goods arrive, tap 'Receive'. Stock goes up, and you scan the IMEI of each phone.
3. Pay now from one of your money accounts, or leave some unpaid. The unpaid part is added to what you owe that supplier.

You can attach a photo of the supplier's paper bill.

s5.text:
Every customer and supplier has a balance.
Customer balance = how much they owe you.
Supplier balance = how much you owe them.

Tap 'Collect' (customer) or 'Pay' (supplier) to settle part or all of it. The money goes into, or out of, the account you choose.

Send a polite WhatsApp reminder for unpaid debts.

s6.text:
Money accounts are the places where money sits: cash drawer, bank, mobile wallet.

Every sale, expense and payment goes into or out of one account, so each balance is always right.

A transfer (for example cash to bank) only moves the shop's own money. It is not income and not an expense, so profit does not change.

Tap an account to see every movement, like a bank statement.

s7.text:
Daily summary: today's sales, repairs, expenses and profit.

Day close: count the cash in the drawer at night. The app shows if anything is short or extra.

Monthly report and Profit and loss work for any dates you pick, and can be saved as PDF or Excel.

Staff cannot see profit or buying prices. Only the owner can.

s8.text:
Settings are what make this a template: shop details, logo, currency, tax, bill layout, product categories and money accounts can all be changed without new code.

Staff: add people as Owner or Staff.

Activity log: shows who did what and when. Records are cancelled, never secretly deleted, so the books always add up.
